notes: Identity verified from the supplied primary Research Article: Inferring Identity From Language: Linguistic Intergroup Bias Informs Social Categorization; Shanette C. Porter, Michelle Rheinschmidt-Same, Jennifer A. Richeson; DOI 10.1177/0956797615612202; Psychological Science 2016, 27(1), 94–102, copyright 2015. Full article text contains methods, results, discussion and references, pp. 94–102. No PDF supplied. Study 3 prints 145 recruited participants, a stopping count of 150, and exclusions of five incomplete respondents, five reporting other political affiliation, and seven with unreported affiliation. No final analytic N or mutually exclusive final-group counts are explicitly printed for this test. The relationship of 145 to the stopping count and exclusions is not explicitly reconciled. No N inferred from degrees of freedom or recruitment/exclusion arithmetic. Unassigned fields are null placeholders, not replacement extractions. The manipulation-check three-way interaction adds future behavior, and friendship analyses concern another outcome; they are distinct from the explicitly named social-category two-way interaction. No p computed from F.
